status: Creative revision for review; existing activation gates retained
creativePlatform: Someone is waiting on that message.
direction: Five human operating stories, each unfolding across five cards. Begin with the person and a recognisable moment, reveal the information gap, make the engineering choice tangible, show responsible behaviour, then invite a real design conversation. These are illustrative situations, not customer stories or testimonials.

brand.accentRule: Use the approved extended accent as a small punctuation, at most 20 percent of designed colour area. Keep actual photography naturally coloured. Official logos only; never generated.
brand.continuity: A broad route or contour line enters and exits at the same edge coordinates across every adjacent pair. It belongs to the landscape: road, irrigation line, river, cable or walking trail. Use split crops or one continuous panorama and a persistent human protagonist; do not repeat one background with five text overlays. Text sits in deliberately reserved calm space. Cards 1 and 5 feel like opening and resolution; 2 to 4 change scale and viewpoint.
brand.copyRule: Headlines ideally 3 to 8 words, one supporting sentence, discreet 01/05 numbering. Primary CTA unchanged. Claim caveats close to relevant capability. No fake quotations, dates, savings or named customers.

carousels.title: The route changes. Someone still needs an answer.
carousels.human: A freight coordinator and the driver they are trying to support, shown as an illustrative working situation.
carousels.continuity: A sweeping road travels left to right through all five cards, becoming a route drawn on the coordinator's desk at the end.

slides.headline: The route just changed.
slides.body: For the person waiting at the next handover, the next update matters.
slides.visual: Close, empathetic driver portrait beside a parked truck; road curves out of the right edge.

slides.headline: So did the coverage.
slides.body: A detour can take a tracker beyond the cellular conditions it was designed around.
slides.visual: Pull wide to the same truck small within a sweeping remote corridor; continuing road establishes the handoff.

slides.headline: Which update cannot wait?
slides.body: Rank the location, delay and exception messages that change a human decision.
slides.visual: Shift to coordinator close-up with sparse, clearly illustrative message categories added deterministically, not a fake live interface.

slides.headline: Give the exception a plan.
slides.body: Design cellular retries, a satellite message path and what happens when neither is available.
slides.visual: Landscape cutaway with two intentional paths and an honest unavailable branch; the road remains the continuous foreground thread.

slides.headline: Bring us the real route.
slides.body: Start with one journey, its critical messages and your device constraints.
slides.visual: Driver and coordinator perspectives resolve in a human engineering discussion over the actual route motif.

carousels.title: The water level cannot read your coverage map.
carousels.human: A farmer checking a remote water installation; practical, calm, knowledgeable.
carousels.continuity: A winding blue-green water line links tank, paddock, sensor, power detail and farm plan; the same farmer anchors the story.

slides.headline: One farm. A lot to watch.
slides.body: A water reading from the far paddock can shape the next job of the day.
slides.visual: Farmer at dawn, tactile hands on fence, bright field light, remote tank visible across the next-card edge.

slides.headline: The tower is somewhere else.
slides.body: Design around the paddock, terrain and sky view where the sensor actually works.
slides.visual: Expansive aerial paddock view with the tank and irrigation contour continuing the prior composition.

slides.headline: This reading changes the day.
slides.body: Separate urgent thresholds from routine readings that can store, batch or retry.
slides.visual: Intimate tank-level or sensor detail and the farmer's considered expression; bold single threshold motif, no fabricated numeric reading.

slides.headline: Make the whole design work.
slides.body: Match message paths to power, antennas and the behaviour required when offline.
slides.visual: Sunlit sensor/solar installation as illustrative hardware, green growth and sweeping water contour; never imply exact 9604 product appearance.

slides.headline: Start with your far paddock.
slides.body: Bring one site's conditions into a Hybrid IoT readiness conversation.
slides.visual: Farmer and technical specialist working over a property plan; water line resolves into the map.

carousels.title: A remote reading. A very human decision.
carousels.human: A field scientist following a remote catchment; attentive observation rather than disaster imagery.
carousels.continuity: The river is a single flowing form across all five cards, moving from real water to a contour and back to the scientist's site plan.

slides.headline: Out here, change is quiet.
slides.body: A remote reading can help someone decide what needs a closer look.
slides.visual: Scientist beside a broad river bend, human foreground, luminous water sweeping into next card.

slides.headline: Which change needs attention?
slides.body: Define which thresholds matter and how quickly the team needs to know.
slides.visual: Macro of the scientist's sampling work and water detail; single bold contour loop gives focus without invented measurement.

slides.headline: Send the part that matters.
slides.body: Design a small, useful exception message and retain detail locally where appropriate.
slides.visual: River narrows into a minimal packet-like grouping, with large calm text space; visual metaphor explicitly distinct from factual dashboard.

slides.headline: Remote still has limits.
slides.body: Plan for power and sky view; a satellite path cannot guarantee delivery.
slides.visual: Wider rugged field station under open sky with terrain occlusion legible, scientist checking the real mounting context.

slides.headline: Bring the site into the design.
slides.body: Use the readiness guide to map the site, payload and reporting priorities.
slides.visual: Scientist and colleague over a catchment map; flowing river becomes a route through their shared plan.

carousels.title: Before someone makes the long drive.
carousels.human: A maintenance technician making a considered remote-site decision, not an alarmist breakdown story.
carousels.continuity: A cable or pipe curves through equipment, diagnostic detail, local-control scene and workshop plan, held at common edge coordinates.

slides.headline: It's a long way out.
slides.body: Before a technician heads to a remote site, the equipment state matters.
slides.visual: Technician beside service vehicle surveying remote installation; human face and warm light counterbalance teal graphics.

slides.headline: What needs their attention now?
slides.body: Choose the fault or threshold messages that change the next maintenance decision.
slides.visual: Move close to gloved hands and equipment inspection; purposeful detail instead of another landscape.

slides.headline: Give critical messages a plan.
slides.body: Define retries and a satellite exception path around urgency, power and payload.
slides.visual: Cable carries into compact illustrated network-path choices beside realistic equipment texture; no automatic-switch promise.

slides.headline: The machine still needs a plan.
slides.body: Keep safe local control independent of connectivity, and make missing data visible.
slides.visual: Technician working on local controls, grounded physical action; clear illustrative unavailable-state symbol near cable.

slides.headline: Start with one real exception.
slides.body: Bring its trigger, response and device constraints to a design review.
slides.visual: Technician and engineer reviewing a workflow; cable motif resolves into a simple drawn exception path.

carousels.title: There is a person behind every check-in.
carousels.human: A competent field worker and a response colleague, both visibly active participants in a safety procedure; no rescue spectacle or implied protective guarantee.
carousels.continuity: A walking trail threads through the worker, device interaction, response colleague and shared safety plan; no glowing forcefield, protective dome or always-on signal.

slides.headline: Someone is expecting your check-in.
slides.body: A field worker and their response team need a clear communications plan.
slides.visual: Warm close portrait of worker preparing at a safe trailhead, with response colleague visually introduced across edge.

slides.headline: Sent. Received. Acknowledged?
slides.body: Define what the worker and response team see at every message state.
slides.visual: Over-shoulder physical device interaction and colleague perspective; status words typeset in finishing, no fake product interface.

slides.headline: Who takes the next step?
slides.body: Set retry, alternate-path and human escalation rules for each event.
slides.visual: Response colleague focused at desk, trail line becomes a procedural connector rather than an asserted delivered signal.

slides.headline: And when no message gets through?
slides.body: Make communication limits visible and define the worker's procedure for that state.
slides.visual: Worker pausing responsibly to follow procedure; calm clear offline condition, no emergency or heroic rescue depiction.

slides.headline: Build the whole safety plan.
slides.body: Review the workflow with technical and safety owners; connectivity is not a safety guarantee.
slides.visual: Worker, safety owner and technical colleague together over a plan; trail unites the human participants.

sourceBasis: Existing campaign-data.js carousel and weekly source copy, read 10 September 2026
qaNotes: No new product specifications or performance claims introduced.
Characters and situations are illustrative; do not label as customer case studies or imply testimonials.
Unchanged CTA destination remains subject to existing destination and release checks.
Expanded review copy should preserve the original detailed engineering questions; concise on-card copy does not replace the technical brief.
Image-generation prompts must exclude all text, logos, watermarks and precise branded hardware; add official branding and typography deterministically.
